mainTopic: בקור חולים: why it matters, its rewards, and how to visit, followed by a side teaching about rain and rivers.
overview: The amud teaches how important בקור חולים is. When no one visited the sick רב חלבו, the חכמים were reminded of רבי עקיבא's student, who recovered only because רבי עקיבא visited. רבי עקיבא then taught that not visiting the sick is like spilling blood. רב דימי adds that a visitor causes the sick person to live, because he prays for him. Someone who stays away never prays at all. רבא kept his illness quiet on the first day and then had it announced so people would pray for him. רב learns from תהלים that a visitor is saved from גיהנם and receives rewards in this world, which leads to a ברייתא about listening to elders, with רחבעם as the example. The גמרא then teaches when to visit and that the שכינה rests above the sick person's bed, so a visitor sits on the ground. Finally it brings another teaching of רבין in the name of רב, about rain and the פרת, and starts a clash between two statements of שמואל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No one visits the sick רב חלבו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב חלבו fell ill and nobody came to visit him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלבו became sick, and no one came to visit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a short story. This line sets up the next step, where someone will rebuke the people for not visiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. The story shows a real failure to do בקור חולים, and this gives the background for the lesson that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'was bad', meaning he was unwell or sick
There was not / there was no one

phrases.english: Rav Chelbo fell ill.
There was no one who came to visit him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story about visiting the sick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רב חלבו was sick and nobody visited him.

steps.title: The story of רבי עקיבא's sick student
steps.stepSummary: Someone reminds the חכמים that a student of רבי עקיבא recovered only because רבי עקיבא visited and had his room cleaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Didn't something like this happen with one of רבי עקיבא's students who got sick? The חכמים did not go in to visit him, but רבי עקיבא did. Because they swept and sprinkled the floor in front of him, he got better. The student said to him: רבי, you brought me back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone rebukes the people who did not visit רב חלבו by telling an older story. A sick student lived only because רבי עקיבא came to visit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that a visit is not only polite. When רבי עקיבא came, he saw what the student needed, and the room was cared for. That care is what made him recover.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that really happened
They swept and sprinkled water on the floor
You brought me back to life

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: He said to them: Wasn't there an incident just like this
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא, from the previous amud, talking to the חכמים who didn't visit רב חלבו.

phrases.aramaic: בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁחָלָה.
phrases.english: with one of the students of Rabbi Akiva who became sick?
The Sages did not go in to visit him,
but Rabbi Akiva went in to visit him,
and because they swept and sprinkled water on the floor before him,
he recovered.
He said to him: My teacher, you have brought me back to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the failure to visit רב חלבו with a story that teaches a lesson.
steps.raayaObject: That visiting the sick can actually save a life.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רבי עקיבא's student, who recovered after רבי עקיבא's visit.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: not visiting is like spilling blood
steps.stepSummary: After the story, רבי עקיבא teaches publicly that whoever does not visit the sick is like someone who spills blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went out and taught: Anyone who does not visit the sick is as if he spills blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא turns the story into a general lesson for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a visit can save a life, staying away can let a sick person die without help. That is why רבי עקיבא compares it to שפיכות דמים.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, not visiting the sick is like שפיכות דמים, because a visit can be what keeps the sick person alive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went out and taught:
Anyone who does not visit the sick
is as though he is spilling blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general lesson from the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Not visiting the sick is like spilling blood.

steps.title: רב דימי: visiting causes life, not visiting causes death
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי teaches that a visitor causes the sick person to live, and someone who doesn't visit causes him to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: Anyone who visits a sick person causes him to live, and anyone who doesn't visit a sick person causes him to die.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רב דימי, gives a strong statement about the power of visiting the sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says more than that visiting is a good deed. He says the visitor actually 'causes' life and the one who stays away 'causes' death. The next steps ask how that can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
That he will live / that he will die

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Anyone who visits the sick person
causes him to live,
and anyone who does not visit the sick person
causes him to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same theme as רבי עקיבא's lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visiting the sick causes him to live, and not visiting causes him to die.

steps.title: How does visiting 'cause' anything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of causing רב דימי means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the way it causes this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רב דימי's words. It is setting up a suggested answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious how a visitor makes someone live or die. The גמרא wants to know the actual mechanism.

keyTerms.meaning: The causing / the way it causes

phrases.english: What is the way it causes this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of רב דימי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How visiting or not visiting causes life or death.

steps.title: A first suggestion: praying for life or for death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a visitor prays for the sick person to live, and someone who doesn't visit prays for him to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: anyone who visits the sick prays for him to live, and anyone who doesn't visit the sick prays for him to die...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer, using the word אילימא ('if you say'). That word tells us this answer is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading makes both halves of רב דימי's statement parallel: each person prays, one for life and one for death. The next step shows why the second half cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you would say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is NOT the conclusion. The word אילימא tells you the גמרא is about to reject it.

phrases.english: If you say: anyone who visits the sick person
prays for mercy on him, that he will live,
and anyone who does not visit the sick person
prays for mercy on him, that he will die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested answer: the visitor prays for life, and the non-visitor prays for death.

steps.title: Would anyone pray for him to die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: it makes no sense that someone who stays away prays for the sick person's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he will die? Could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested answer. No normal person prays for a sick person to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the suggestion is absurd, so that reading of רב דימי must be wrong. Now the גמרא needs a different explanation of how not visiting 'causes' death.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (meaning: that's impossible)

phrases.english: That he will die? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that a non-visitor prays for the sick person to die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody would pray for a sick person's death, so this cannot be what רב דימי meant.

steps.title: The non-visitor simply doesn't pray at all
steps.stepSummary: The real meaning is that someone who doesn't visit doesn't pray for the sick person at all, neither for life nor for death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anyone who doesn't visit a sick person doesn't pray for him, neither that he should live nor that he should die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct explanation. Staying away 'causes' death because the person never prays for the sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The visitor sees the sick person and prays for him, and that prayer can help. The one who stays away loses that chance, so his absence is counted as causing death even though he wished no harm.
steps.whatToRemember: A visitor helps the sick person through his prayers. Someone who doesn't visit 'causes' death only because he never prays at all.

phrases.english: Rather: anyone who does not visit a sick person
does not pray for mercy on him,
neither that he will live nor that he will die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion with the correct explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the second half of רב דימי's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The non-visitor actively prays for death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The non-visitor doesn't pray at all, and losing that prayer is what 'causes' death.

steps.title: רבא keeps his illness private on the first day
steps.stepSummary: On the first day he was sick, רבא told his household not to tell anyone, so that his מזל would not be harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day that רבא was sick, he said to them: Don't tell anyone, so that my luck won't be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבא behaved when he became sick. At first he kept it quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading news of an illness too early could harm a person's מזל. So on the first day, before it was serious, רבא wanted it kept private.

phrases.english: Rava, on the first day that he was sick,
said to them: Don't reveal it to anyone,
so that his luck will not be harmed.
phrases.notes: 'His luck' means רבא's own luck. He is speaking about himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about how a sick person should handle news of his illness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day of illness, keep it private so as not to harm one's מזל.

steps.title: After that, רבא has his illness announced publicly
steps.stepSummary: From the second day on, רבא had his illness announced in the market, so that his enemies would rejoice and his friends would pray for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on he said to them: Go out and announce it in the market. Whoever hates me can rejoice over me, and it is written: 'When your enemy falls, do not rejoice...' And whoever loves me should pray for mercy for me.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first day, רבא changed course and wanted everyone to know he was sick, because both his enemies and his friends could help him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His friends would pray for him. Even his enemies' happiness could help: the פסוק warns against rejoicing when an enemy falls, so their joy might lead ה׳ to turn His anger away from רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא kept his illness quiet on the first day and then made it public, so people would pray for him.

phrases.english: From then on, he said to them:
Go out and announce it in the marketplace,
so that whoever hates me can rejoice over me,
and it is written: 'When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, etc.'
phrases.notes: משלי 24:17. The next פסוק says ה׳ may then turn His anger away from the one who fell.

phrases.english: and whoever loves me should pray for mercy for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's story with what he did after the first day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the first day, publicize the illness so that friends will pray and enemies' joy may lead ה׳ to turn away His anger.

steps.title: רב: whoever visits the sick is saved from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that visiting the sick saves a person from the judgment of גיהנם, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Anyone who visits the sick is saved from the judgment of גיהנם, as it says: 'Happy is he who considers the poor; on the day of evil ה׳ will rescue him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new teaching about the reward for בקור חולים and brings a פסוק to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק talks about a 'דל' (poor person) and a 'day of evil'. רב will explain in the next steps that דל means a sick person and 'evil' means גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: Considers / pays attention to the poor (or weak)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה
phrases.english: Rav said: Anyone who visits the sick person
is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom,
as it is stated: 'Happy is he who considers the poor;'
'on the day of evil, ה׳ will rescue him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the reward for visiting the sick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever visits the sick is saved from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.title: Proof that 'דל' means a sick person
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים show that the word דל can mean someone who is sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'דל' means only a sick person, as it says: 'He will cut me off from illness (מדלה).' Or from this פסוק: 'Why are you so sick (דל), son of the king, morning after morning...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first part of רב's reading: the 'דל' in תהלים is a sick person, so the פסוק is about visiting the sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חזקיהו's prayer during his illness, מדלה means sickness. In the story of אמנון, he is called דל because he looked sick. Either פסוק shows that דל can mean ill.

keyTerms.meaning: X means nothing other than Y

phrases.english: 'Poor' (dal) means nothing other than a sick person,
as it is stated: 'He will cut me off from illness,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:12, from חזקיהו's prayer when he was sick.

phrases.english: Alternatively, from this verse:
'Why are you so sick (dal), son of the king,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:4, said to אמנון, דוד's son.

phrases.english: 'morning after morning, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word דל in רב's פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That דל in תהלים 41:2 means a sick person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 38:12 (מדלה), or alternatively שמואל ב 13:4 (דל בן המלך).

steps.title: Proof that 'רעה' means גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in משלי shows that the 'day of evil' is the day the wicked are punished, meaning גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Evil' means only גיהנם, as it says: 'ה׳ made everything for His purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second part of רב's reading: the 'day of evil' is גיהנם. This completes the proof that visiting the sick saves from גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי says the wicked are set aside for 'the day of evil', which is their punishment in גיהנם. So 'ה׳ will rescue him on the day of evil' means He saves the one who visits the sick from גיהנם.
steps.whatToRemember: רב reads תהלים 41:2 as: whoever pays attention to the sick (דל) will be saved by ה׳ from גיהנם (יום רעה).

phrases.english: 'Evil' means nothing other than Gehinnom,
as it is stated: 'ה׳ made everything for His purpose,'
'and even the wicked for the day of evil.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second key word of רב's פסוק and completes the derivation.
steps.raayaObject: That יום רעה in תהלים 41:2 means גיהנם.

steps.title: What is the reward for visiting the sick?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reward a person gets for visiting a sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone visited a sick person, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what does someone get for visiting the sick? This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question picks up from רב's teaching in step 11 about visiting the sick. As we will see right away, the question seems strange, because the answer was already given.

phrases.english: And if one visited, what is his reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reward for visiting the sick, the topic of רב's teaching in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward does someone get for visiting a sick person?

steps.title: But we already know the reward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why it asked, since רב already said the visitor is saved from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his reward?! It is just as was said: he is saved from the judgment of גיהנם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by its own question. The answer was already given in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that visiting the sick saves a person from the judgment of גיהנם. So asking 'what is his reward' seems pointless. The question has to mean something else.

phrases.english: What is his reward?!
It is as he said: he is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question of step 14 as already answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reward was already stated by רב: being saved from גיהנם, so there is no reason to ask.

steps.title: The question is about reward in this world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question was about the visitor's reward in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is: what is his reward in this world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes its question: it is not about the next world, but about this world. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being saved from גיהנם is a reward after death. The new question asks what good things the visitor gets while he is still alive.

phrases.english: Rather: what is his reward in this world?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by narrowing the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to ask about the visitor's reward in general, which was already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question asks about his reward in this world.

steps.title: Four rewards in this world from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים is explained as four rewards in this world for the one who visits the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: "God will guard him and keep him alive, he will be praised in the land, and do not give him over to the will of his enemies." "God will guard him" from the יצר הרע. "And keep him alive" from suffering. "He will be praised in the land" means everyone will feel honored to be with him. "Do not give him over to his enemies" means he will get good friends like נעמן's, who helped heal his צרעת, and not bad friends like רחבעם's, who caused his kingdom to split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with the next פסוק in תהלים, and explains each part of it as a different reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק continues from the one רב used in step 11. Each phrase becomes one reward: protection from the יצר הרע, from suffering, honor from people, and good friends. The good and bad friends are shown through נעמן and רחבעם.

keyTerms.meaning: feel honored to be with him

steps.whyThisMatters: The example of רחבעם's bad advisers leads straight into the ברייתא in the next step.

phrases.english: "God will guard him and keep him alive,
and he will be praised in the land,
and do not give him over to the will of his enemies."
"God will guard him": from the evil inclination;
"and keep him alive": from suffering;
"and he will be praised in the land": that everyone will feel honored by him;
"and do not give him over to the will of his enemies":
that friends like Naaman's will come his way,
who healed his tzaraas,
phrases.notes: נעמן's companions gave him good advice that led to his cure. See מלכים ב 5.

phrases.english: and friends like Rechavam's will not come his way,
who split his kingdom.
phrases.notes: See מלכים א 12. Their advice made most of the tribes break away from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the narrowed question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In this world the visitor is protected from the יצר הרע and from suffering, is honored by all, and gets good friends instead of bad ones.
steps.whatToRemember: Visiting the sick saves you from גיהנם (step 11), and in this world it brings four rewards: protection from the יצר הרע, protection from suffering, honor, and good friends.

steps.title: Listen to elders, not youths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that you should follow the elders' advice over the youths', using רחבעם as the example.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: If youths tell you "build" and elders tell you "tear down," listen to the elders and not to the youths. The building of youths is really tearing down, and the tearing down of elders is really building. A sign for this: רחבעם son of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just mentioned רחבעם's bad advisers, it brings a ברייתא that uses רחבעם as an example of following the wrong advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young advisers' plan looks like building but ends in ruin. The elders' plan looks like giving something up but ends up building. רחבעם listened to the young men, and his kingdom split.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: "Build" and "tear down" are not about real buildings. They describe advice that looks helpful or harmful at first.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
If youths tell you "build"
and elders say "tear down,"
listen to the elders and do not listen to the youths,
because the building of youths is tearing down,
and the tearing down of elders is building.
And a sign for the matter: Rechavam son of Shlomo.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of רחבעם's bad advisers in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Follow the elders' advice over the youths'. What looks like building from youths is ruin, and what looks like tearing down from elders is building.

steps.title: When not to visit a sick person
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says not to visit a sick person in the first three or last three hours of the day, so the visitor will still pray for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: A person should not visit a sick person in the first three hours of the day or in the last three hours of the day, so that he does not stop thinking about praying for him. In the first three hours, the sick person feels relieved. In the last three hours, his weakness gets stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to visiting the sick and gives a practical rule about timing, then explains the reason for each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal of the visit includes praying for the sick person. In the morning he looks better, so the visitor may think there is no need to pray. In the late afternoon he looks worse, so the visitor may lose hope and think prayer won't help.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a main purpose of visiting the sick is to be moved to pray for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Visit a sick person in the middle hours of the day, when you will see that he needs prayer and that prayer can still help.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
A person should not visit a sick person
not in the first three hours
and not in the last three hours of the day,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לַיסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִן רַחֲמֵי.
phrases.english: so that he does not take his mind off praying for mercy.
The first three hours: he feels relieved.
The last ones: his weakness grows strong.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to visiting the sick after the side topic of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not visit a sick person in the first or last three hours of the day, so the visitor will still pray for him.

steps.title: God Himself feeds the sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבין quotes רב that הקב״ה Himself sustains the sick person, learned from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין said in the name of רב: How do we know that הקב״ה feeds the sick person? Because it says: "ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the sick: God Himself takes care of feeding a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יִסְעָדֶנּוּ is read as "He will sustain him," meaning give him food and strength. So the פסוק is saying that God personally looks after a sick person's needs. This fits the larger topic of how special a sick person is.

keyTerms.meaning: He will support or sustain him

phrases.english: Ravin said that Rav said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
feeds the sick person?
As it says:
"ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 41:4. "Support" here means God gives him food and strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זָן אֶת הַחוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about visiting the sick, this time about God's care for the sick person himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה Himself sustains the sick person, as learned from "ה׳ יסעדנו על ערש דוי".

steps.title: The Divine Presence rests above the sick person's bed
steps.stepSummary: רבין quotes רב that the שכינה rests above the sickbed, learned from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין also said in the name of רב: How do we know that the שכינה rests above the sick person's bed? Because it says: "ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering."
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same פסוק: God's Presence is right above the sick person's bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the focus is on the word "upon" (עַל) the bed. It is read as God being right there over the bed. The same פסוק gives two different lessons.
steps.confusionAlert: Both teachings use the exact same פסוק. The first reads it as God feeding the sick person; the second reads "on the bed" as God's Presence being above the bed.

phrases.english: And Ravin said that Rav said:
From where do we know that the Divine Presence rests
above the bed of the sick person?
As it says: "ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before. Now the point is the word "on," meaning ה׳ is right there over the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבִין אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שְׁרוּיָה לְמַעְלָה מִמִּטָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַחוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same speakers from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה rests above the sick person's bed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: the visitor sits on the ground
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a visitor should not sit on a bed, bench or chair, but on the ground, because the שכינה is above the sickbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same idea: Someone who visits a sick person should not sit on the bed, a bench, or a chair. Instead he wraps himself and sits on the ground, because the שכינה rests above the sick person's bed, as it says: "ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב's teaching that the שכינה is above the sickbed, and turns it into a practical rule for visitors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שכינה is above the bed, it is not respectful for a visitor to sit up high near that spot. So the ברייתא tells him to sit low, on the ground, wrapped respectfully. This shows רב's teaching has a real halachic result.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way, in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule about how to behave when visiting the sick, built directly on the idea that the שכינה is present there.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who goes in to visit a sick person

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֵשֵׁב לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: should not sit, not on the bed
and not on a bench
and not on a chair.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִתְעַטֵּף וְיוֹשֵׁב עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: Rather, he wraps himself and sits on the ground,
because the Divine Presence rests
above the bed of the sick person,
as it says: "ה׳ will support him on the bed of suffering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21 with a ברייתא that says the same idea and draws a practical rule from it.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that the שכינה rests above the sick person's bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that tells visitors to sit on the ground for this exact reason, using the same פסוק.

steps.title: Rain in ארץ ישראל shows up in the river פרת
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רבין in the name of רב: when it rains in ארץ ישראל, the river פרת is the great witness to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין also said in the name of רב: When it rains in the West, ארץ ישראל, the great witness to it is the river פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא has been quoting רבין in the name of רב, it adds another of his teachings, this time on a new topic: rain and rivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is saying that rainwater from ארץ ישראל flows into the פרת. So when the פרת rises in בבל, it is a sign that it rained in ארץ ישראל. This is not about the sick at all; it comes up only because of who said it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a link to visiting the sick. This teaching is here only because it is another statement of רבין in the name of רב.

phrases.english: And Ravin said that Rav said:
Rain in the West:
phrases.notes: "The West" is ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל, where the גמרא was being learned.

phrases.english: the great witness is the Euphrates.
phrases.notes: When the river rises, it shows that it rained in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבִין אָמַר רַב: מִטְרָא בְּמַעְרְבָא סָהֲדָא רַבָּה פְּרָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only by being another teaching of רבין in the name of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain in ארץ ישראל makes the פרת rise, so the river is a witness to that rain.

steps.title: רב disagrees with שמואל about where rivers get their water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב's view argues with שמואל, who said a river grows from its own banks, not from distant rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with שמואל, because שמואל said: A river is blessed from its banks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב's teaching about the פרת does not fit with what שמואל said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says rain far away in ארץ ישראל makes the פרת rise. שמואל says a river's water increases from what feeds into it along its banks. So they have two different views of where a river's extra water comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: is blessed, meaning it gets more water

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:
A river is blessed from its banks.
phrases.notes: A river grows from the water flowing into it along its own banks, not from rain far away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that רב's statement in step 23 conflicts with a statement of שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל holds that a river's increase comes from its own banks, unlike רב.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that one statement of שמואל seems to clash with another of his statements, about purifying in flowing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one statement of שמואל disagrees with another statement of שמואל, because שמואל said: Water does not purify when it is flowing... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now finds a contradiction inside שמואל's own words. It sets this up by quoting a second statement of his, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, שמואל said a river grows from its banks. Now the גמרא quotes his other rule about when flowing water can purify, which seems to assume rain does add to rivers. The full statement and the explanation of the clash come on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not רב against שמואל anymore. Now it is שמואל against שמואל, two of his own statements that seem to clash.

phrases.english: And Shmuel's statement disagrees with Shmuel's,
for Shmuel said:
Water does not purify when flowing
phrases.notes: This sentence isn't finished yet. It continues on the next amud, where we see why it clashes with his other statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב against שמואל to an apparent clash between two statements of שמואל himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that a river is blessed from its banks (step 24).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another rule of שמואל about purifying in flowing water seems to assume something different about where river water comes from. The full statement is completed on the next amud.
